    Split-basic presentations of radical quotients #

    A two-sided ideal contained in the Jacobson radical does not change the semisimple quotient. This file makes that fact concrete for the chosen primitive idempotents used by SplitBasicIdempotents: their images form the corresponding chosen split-basic presentation of the quotient algebra.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.TwoSidedIdeal.quotient_mk_mem_jacobson_iff {A : Type v} [Ring A] (I : TwoSidedIdeal A) (hI : TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal I ≤ Ring.jacobson A) (a : A) :
    (Ideal.Quotient.mk (TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal I)) a ∈ Ring.jacobson (A ⧸ TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal I) ↔ a ∈ Ring.jacobson A

    Membership in the Jacobson radical of a quotient by a smaller radical ideal is detected before passing to the quotient.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.TwoSidedIdeal.quotient_mk_not_mem_jacobson_sq {A : Type v} [Ring A] (I : TwoSidedIdeal A) (hI : TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal I ≤ Ring.jacobson A) (hI₂ : TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal I ≤ Ring.jacobson A * Ring.jacobson A) (a : A) (ha : a ∉ Ring.jacobson A * Ring.jacobson A) :
    (Ideal.Quotient.mk (TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal I)) a ∉ Ring.jacobson (A ⧸ TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal I) * Ring.jacobson (A ⧸ TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal I)

    Quotienting by an ideal contained in the radical square preserves nonmembership in the first radical layer.

          The BGRS distributive Hom structure descends to every quotient by an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical. The primitive-projective quotient functor is full and its object map is an equivalence on the chosen labels.
